title: clarify-retry-and-idempotency-metrics-across-api-surface
author: Ethan Brooks
release_notes: Clarify and standardize Retry-After semantics and idempotency telemetry. Introduces X-Redwood-Retry-After and X-Redwood-Idempotency-Status headers, normalizes 429/503 error envelope to include machine-readable backoff_hint and idempotency_state, and exposes new Prometheus meters for idempotency collisions and retry-window distribution.
description:
Context and motivation: During recent incidents and customer reports, we observed inconsistent Retry-After semantics across the OpenAI-compat adapter and the direct Redwood API: some callers saw coarse second-level Retry-After headers while streamed tool callers received only opaque 429 bodies. This caused client-side backoff thrashing and made it hard to correlate idempotency collisions in telemetry. This PR standardizes the surface contract and adds observability to make post-incident analysis straightforward.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Standardizes Retry-After exposure, surfaces idempotency resolution state via headers, normalizes machine-readable error envelopes for 429/503 with a backoff_hint token, and emits new metrics for idempotency collisions and retry-window histograms. Also updates SDK shims and documentation to match the new contract.

Checklist: 
- [x] Define and implement X-Redwood-Retry-After header (RFC-3339 delta and millisecond token forms)
- [x] Add X-Redwood-Idempotency-Status header (values: accepted|replayed|collision|broken)
- [x] Extend 429/503 error_envelope to include backoff_hint and idempotency_state fields (machine-readable JSON)
- [x] Emit telemetry: idempotency_collision_count, idempotency_resolution_latency_ms histogram, retry_window_seconds histogram
- [x] Update OpenAI-compat shim to forward new headers for compatibility mode
- [x] Update Python and TypeScript SDK helpers with higher-level retry/backoff wrappers that read the new headers
- [x] Add integration tests covering streaming tool replays and idempotency collision attribution
- [x] Update docs for API surface and migration notes

Commits (high level):
- f8c11d3  Implement X-Redwood-Retry-After header format and parsing in gateway
- a4b9e20  Normalize error_envelope for 429/503 and add backoff_hint tokens
- 3d2f7b1  Add idempotency session manager metrics and collision handling hooks
- b7f2aa8  SDK: python/ts helpers to respect server backoff_hint and idempotency status
- 5c4e9f0  Tests + docs: integration test and docs page for migration and examples

Files changed (high level):
- services/gateway/src/handlers/retry_policy.rs: adds parsing logic for both numeric Retry-After and opaque backoff tokens and chooses which to emit based on client capability header. Small code snippet added to pick RFC delta or server-token form.
- services/streaming/src/idempotency/session_manager.rs: record resolution outcomes and expose state transitions (accepted -> replayed -> collision). Adds a lightweight in-memory histogram for resolution latencies.
- services/streaming/src/protocol/error_envelope.rs: change error envelope shape to { code, message, backoff_hint?, idempotency_state? } and add helpers for Marshaler/Unmarshaler.
- console/docs/api/retry_and_idempotency.md: new doc covering header semantics, SDK migration snippets, and example client behavior for streams and function calls.
- sdk updates: helpers in Python and TS that read X-Redwood-Retry-After and X-Redwood-Idempotency-Status, and expose a RetryPolicy object for callers to integrate with their event loops.

Review conversation summary: 
- Priya Kapoor: "Thanks — the telemetry additions look good. Two requests: make the backoff_hint token expire (we do) and ensure the SDK helpers provide a non-blocking async sleep path for streaming clients."
- Author (Ethan): "Added TTL to backoff tokens and switched the Python helper to an asyncio-friendly sleep that drains without blocking the event loop. See commit b7f2aa8."
- Liam Chen: "Please confirm we won't break existing clients that only parse numeric Retry-After. Suggest emitting both X-Redwood-Retry-After (RFC delta in seconds) and X-Redwood-Retry-Token when available."
- Author: "Gateway now emits both when the backoff_hint is present: RFC delta for basic clients and Retry-Token for advanced clients; documentation updated with examples."
- Sofia Martinez (approval): "Test coverage is solid and docs are clear. Approving after minor nits fixed in code comments."

CI and rollout notes: 
- CI: full test matrix passed (unit, integration, lint). E2E flaky in first run due to timing assumptions; fixed by making test tolerances explicit.
- Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag 'feature.api.backoff_v2' and will be enabled by gradual canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) to observe idempotency_collision_count before wide release.

Compatibility and migration: 
- Backward compatible: existing clients that read numeric Retry-After will continue to get a numeric delta when a server-side estimate is available. For stream/tool callers, clients that understand Retry-Token will be able to correlate server-side idempotency sessions and avoid duplicate tool execution.
- Telemetry: New Prometheus metrics added; Grafana dashboard provisioning file included so SRE can watch idempotency collisions and retry-window percentiles during canary.

Why this is different from prior work: previous PRs adjusted Retry-After formats or stream framing, but did not pair the header-level contract with explicit idempotency-state telemetry or emit a machine-readable backoff token that can be used by streaming clients to deterministically defer replays. This PR ties the contract to observability so we can quantify improvements in client behavior post-release.

Follow-ups: 
- Export backoff_hint correlation id to traces for end-to-end debugging (ENG-4910).
- Consider adding a server-side advisory for recommended jitter windows based on load profiles (ENG-4932).

Merge: Squash merge after approvals and CI green.

Testing notes: Integration test spins up a small streaming harness that simulates duplicate tool invocations and asserts that idempotency_state transitions to 'replayed' for the second attempt, and that idempotency_collision_count increments exactly once when true conflicts occur.

Contact: For migration questions, ping @ethan.brooks or open ENG-4872 in Linear.
